segments.t: At the bar in Claude Monet, Kostya accidentally drops an expensive bottle of wine right in front of Dmitry Nagiyev, earning a painful fine that leaves Nastya furious.
Молодец, просто отличная работа!
Сам разбил, сам и заплатишь.
Понял, я всё оплачу.
И ещё штраф сверху!
Костя, ты совсем с ума сошёл?
Давай просто деньги рвать будем!
У нас же денег так много!
Тихо, Настя, только не кричи.
Здравствуйте, мы тут в лифте застряли.
Нажмите кнопку и вызовите мастера.
Мы уже нажимали, никто не отвечает.
Позвоните, пожалуйста, нашему другу.
Давайте номер, только быстрее.
Let's examine each line of Kostya's costly mistake at the bar.
Молодец, просто отличная работа!
'Well done, simply a great job!' With the shift and wine at stake, Nagiyev reacts without holding back. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat.
Сам разбил, сам и заплатишь.
'You broke it yourself, you will pay for it yourself.' Saying that Kostya broke it themselves Kostya will pay for it themselves is how Nagiyev sets the tone with Kostya.
Понял, я всё оплачу.
'Got it, I will pay for everything.' Once got it he will pay for everything, Kostya can finally tell Nagiyev what he means.
И ещё штраф сверху!
'And a fine on top of that too!' Over the moment and the wine, Nagiyev lets his real feelings show. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat.
Костя, ты совсем с ума сошёл?
'Kostya, have you completely lost your mind?' By asking whether Kostya completely lost Kostya's mind, Nastya presses Kostya for a straight answer.
Давай просто деньги рвать будем!

'Let's just tear up our money then!' Once they should just tear up their money then, Nastya makes sure Kostya hears every word. Starting with "davay" is the everyday Russian way to say "come on, let us do this".
У нас же денег так много!

'We have so much money, after all!' Nastya declares that they have so much money after all as the tension in the room peaks. In Russian you say "by me" or "with us" rather than "I have", so the situation sits right with the person.
Тихо, Настя, только не кричи.
'Quiet, Nastya, just do not shout.' Kostya reminds Nagiyev that quiet Nastya just do not shout before the moment passes.
Здравствуйте, мы тут в лифте застряли.
'Hello, we are stuck in the elevator here.' Because they are stuck in the elevator here, Nastya treats the matter as settled.
Нажмите кнопку и вызовите мастера.
'Press the button and call the technician.' With the moment and wine in play, Kostya keeps this short reply brisk and direct.
Мы уже нажимали, никто не отвечает.
'We already pressed it, nobody answers.' Nastya mentions that they already pressed it nobody answers so Kostya sees what is at stake.
Позвоните, пожалуйста, нашему другу.
'Please call our friend for us.' By calling their friend for them, Nastya keeps her side of the story grounded.
Давайте номер, только быстрее.

'Give me the number, just make it quick.' Realizing that Nagiyev should give him the number just make it quick changes how Kostya handles the situation. Starting with "davay" is the everyday Russian way to say "come on, let us do this". Now let's hear the whole scene again from start to finish.
Молодец, просто отличная работа!
Сам разбил, сам и заплатишь.
Понял, я всё оплачу.
И ещё штраф сверху!
Костя, ты совсем с ума сошёл?
Давай просто деньги рвать будем!
У нас же денег так много!

Нажмите кнопку и вызовите мастера.

Давайте номер, только быстрее.
Listen for how Russian says 'got it!' or 'understood!' using the single past-tense verb 'ponyal' for a male speaker. See you next time!
До завтра!
